The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 84 from Travis Head, complemented by a commanding 166-run stand between Travis Head and M Labuschagne that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.0 RPO. Sri Lanka's bowling response was spearheaded by RAS Lakmal (5/73), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Reaching 323/10 (106.2 ov), Australia's innings completed the first-innings exchange (179 Runs (Australia)), shaping the strategic contours for the second half of the Test.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Brisbane Cricket Ground commenced with high tactical intensity as Sri Lanka posted 144/10 (56.4 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Australia countered with 323/10 (106.2 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: Pat Cummins (6/23), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Pat Cummins delivered a masterclass for Australia (10 Wickets), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Australia 54%) and allowing Australia to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Sri Lanka faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Australia's bowling unit, bolstered by RAS Lakmal (31 Runs & 5 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Australia won by innings & 40 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Australia's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Sri Lanka produced fighting phases, Australia won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
